subtype: Approach: iterating from feedback and usage numbers [Revision]
passage: “Jasleen, sit down. I'll tell you how a number saved my school magazine site. I'm Kiran. I was sixteen and proud of it: four pages, and I'd put a little visit counter at the bottom, just for fun. After a month I looked. The home page had a hundred visits. The third page, my classmates' poetry, had two. Two! I was hurt. I asked my cousin why. My cousin said, ‘I never found it. It's hidden under More.’ I hadn't thought of that. I moved poetry to the front page, right under the title. Within a week it had thirty-one visits. The poems hadn't changed. Only where they sat.”

qa.q: How many visits did the poetry page get in the first month?
How did Kiran feel on learning why nobody opened the poetry page?
qa.a: Hurt at first, then surprised and a little embarrassed that the fault was the design and not the poems.

qa.q: Which choice in the story turned things around, and why?
qa.a: Asking why instead of guessing: the cousin's answer showed the page was hidden, so moving it to the front page fixed it.

qa.q: How might Kiran's cousin have felt when asked?
qa.a: The cousin was probably glad to be asked and to give honest feedback, and pleased to see the change made.

grounding: An elder recalls noticing from visit counts that nobody opened page three, asking why, moving it to the homepage and seeing visits rise.
